sources.title: Effects of non-rapid eye movement sleep on the cortical synaptic expression of GluA1-containing AMPA receptors
sources.authors: Squarcio F, Tononi G, Cirelli C
sources.usage: Core data: GluA1 43.8% higher after SD; p-GluA1(845) 78.9% higher; 5h recovery normalizes GluA1; REM deprivation insufficient

sources.title: Slow-wave sleep drives sleep-dependent renormalization of synaptic AMPA receptor levels in the hypothalamus
sources.authors: Liu J, Niethard N, Lun Y, Dimithard S, Ehrlich I, Born J, Hallschmid M
sources.usage: Hypothalamus GluA1 142.7% of sleep after SD; SWS drives renormalization; spindle density positively predicts GluA1 (memory consolidation side); CDK5/Homer1a as candidate mechanism

sources.title: Homer1a drives homeostatic scaling-down of excitatory synapses during sleep
sources.authors: Diering GH, Nirujogi RS, Roth RH, Worley PF, Pandey A, Huganir RL
sources.usage: Core Homer1a mechanism: NA excludes from PSD; adenosine promotes entry via A1R; mGluR5-IP3R complex disruption; GluA1/GluA2 PSD reduction; memory specificity improved by sleep scaling-down

sources.title: Remembering and forgetting in sleep: Selective synaptic plasticity during sleep driven by scaling factors Homer1a and Arc
sources.usage: Arc inverse synaptic tagging mechanism: Arc binds dephospho-CaMKIIβ (silent synapses), excluded from phospho-CaMKIIβ (LTP synapses); Arc-Homer1a cooperation

sources.title: Loss of Arc attenuates the behavioral and molecular responses for sleep homeostasis in mice
sources.authors: Suzuki A, Yanagisawa M, Greene RW
sources.usage: Arc KO mice: reduced sleep rebound; Arc 2.5x increase in SD; nuclear Arc suppresses GluA1 mRNA; bidirectional Arc role in synaptic strengthening/weakening

sources.title: Wake-active brainstem GABA neurons signal sleep pressure by upregulating AMPA receptors to drive recovery sleep
sources.authors: Ba W, Harding EC, Nollet M, Tossell K, Li LL, Wong S, Wisden W, Franks NP
sources.usage: Brainstem GABA neurons upregulate GluA1 AMPA receptors after SD to drive recovery sleep - AMPA receptors as sleep pressure sensor (opposite direction to cortical downscaling)

sources.title: Sleep and the price of plasticity: from synaptic and cellular homeostasis to memory consolidation and integration
sources.usage: SHY framework; spontaneous activity renormalizes synaptic strength during sleep; functional rationale for downscaling

sources.title: Sleep function and synaptic homeostasis
sources.usage: SHY original hypothesis; slow-wave activity as synaptic downscaling signal

sources.title: Homer1a and mGluR1/5 Signaling in Homeostatic Sleep Drive and Output
sources.authors: Martin SC, Monroe SK, Diering GH
sources.usage: Homer1a uncouples mGluR1/5 from IP3R during sleep; awake-type vs sleep-type signaling modes

sources.title: Clathrin adaptor AP2 and NSF interact with overlapping sites of GluR2 and play distinct roles in AMPA receptor trafficking and hippocampal LTD
sources.authors: Lee SH, Liu L, Wang YT, Bhattacharyya S, Bhaskaran S, Bhattacharyya S, Bhaskaran S
sources.usage: Classical AMPA receptor endocytosis via GluR2-AP2 interaction; NSF competition for same site; foundational LTD mechanism context
